bottleneck: We know common variants alter drug metabolism, efficacy, and toxicity, yet pharmacogenomic testing is rarely integrated into prescribing. Evidence gaps persist for most drug-gene pairs, clinical decision support is patchy across health systems, and physicians lack training to act on results confidently. The science of who responds to which drug outpaces the medicine of actually using it, and testing ordered reactively after an adverse event arrives too late to prevent harm.
current_state: Testing exists for a handful of high-impact pairs (e.g., CYP2C19/clopidogrel, TPMT/thiopurines) but remains optional in most health systems. Preemptive panel testing before prescribing is rare outside academic centers.

title: Pharmacogenomics known but unused in prescribing
why_it_blocks: Adverse drug reactions hospitalize millions yearly, many predictable from genetics. The implementation gap between genomic knowledge and clinical workflow wastes lives and money daily, for a test that costs a fraction of one hospitalization.
